memo.verdict: Bearish; park; medium conviction (the direction of the earnings and of the multiple is well evidenced; the size of any copper move is not). The park rule applies on two of its four grounds: management (RA 3, E 1, BB 4) at D and business quality (E 2, BB 2) at D; predictability (RA 8, E 2, BB 4) is C and trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4) is B; nothing in the record argues against parking. All four Building Blocks are D and all four are D for one connected reason: a symmetric bet on one exogenous price (copper), taken at that price's record, on a multiple above its own centre, in a company whose owner's next capital decision is unknowable. The record's one-line bet it declines: that copper rises another third from a record while a state owner spends the proceeds wisely. What would re-open the case: a copper price sustained above USD 16,000 per tonne with the shares below PLN 260; or a change of owner behaviour (an equity-aligned chief executive; a withdrawn polyhalite commitment) with the multiple below 7.4x. The 'Modal return' is negative at both horizons: PLN 252.9 of value including cash returns at 2028-04-07 (-17.0 percent a year) and PLN 275.1 at 2029-10-07 (-6.3 percent a year) from PLN 334.6 on 2026-10-07.
case: - The external force is real, sector-wide, structural and already in the accounts. Copper at records on a forecast 2026 deficit of 350,000 tonnes and inventories of 15 days of consumption; grids, electric vehicles and data centres give more than two years' visibility. Q2 2026 revenue rose 49 percent and FY2026 consensus EPS rose 131.8 percent in twelve months. A force the sell-side has modelled is not a force with further to travel.

- KGHM captures the force through price alone. Volume is flat at over 730,000 tonnes a year guided to 2030; the domestic cost position is upper-half; each increment of the copper price is shared with the zloty, the wage bill and the extraction tax formula. The leverage (66 percent of EPS per 10 percent of copper) is symmetric and, from a record, more likely to work downwards.

- The internal change since January 2026 points the wrong way for a minority shareholder: an administrator-profile chief executive with no mining record; a PLN 32 billion capital plan; a 12-to-14-year fertiliser mine; a USD 2 to 5 billion acquisition search at the top of the cycle, with a record of overpayment (Quadra FNX in 2012; Sierra Gorda's USD 3.9 billion overrun and PLN 3.66 billion impairment). The sell-side read the strategy as the end of capex containment: a downgrade, a target multiple cut one standard deviation to 5.9x, Underweights from 10 percent to 36 percent.
counter_case: At its strongest: KGHM is the cheapest copper producer in the world on EV/EBITDA, 4.1x spot 2026 and 4.6x 2027 against Western peers at 10 to 11x. Its balance sheet is at 0.4x net debt to EBITDA with a 2.0x covenant. Its one world-class asset, Sierra Gorda, is first-quartile at a C1 of USD 0.72 per pound, has repaid over USD 1 billion of owner loans in 2021 to 2025 and is sanctioned to grow 30 percent. Copper inventories are the lowest in history (ex-US cover of 2.5 days; a 2026 deficit near 350,000 tonnes); Deutsche Bank sees USD 22,050 per tonne by Q2 2027 and a plausible Chinese stock-out. The Polish state has just cut the extraction tax. The sell-side has already taken a 13 percent downgrade to 2027 EBITDA on spot prices, the Underweight share is 36 percent, and consensus revenue of PLN 47,759 million for FY2027 assumes no further price rise, so the bad news is in the numbers. The technical picture is a proven Stage 2 at the 86th percentile of relative strength. Every governance objection the record makes has been true for a decade during which the shares have also doubled. With a 66 percent EPS sensitivity to a 10 percent copper move, if copper does what the bulls say, EPS could exceed PLN 50 (UBS has PLN 58.54 for FY2027) and the shares could reach PLN 450 to 467 (UBS's target; Morgan Stanley's bull case) on no re-rating at all; FY2027 EPS would then sit far above the PLN 36 consensus and the 'Demand Inflection' pattern would be crisp, still in its early innings. The risks are known, priced and bounded: the discount to peers already carries the governance and strategy risk.

The record's response: it concedes the balance sheet, the tightness of the copper market, the quality of Sierra Gorda, the price momentum, and that the EV/EBITDA discount is genuine and large. It holds its view because the framework's question is about the modal path and not the bull path: on the modal path the earnings fall and the multiple sits above its own centre; the EV/EBITDA discount is a cross-sectional fact that has not closed in ten years and whose closing needs the owner to change, not the copper price; the sell-side's own re-rating arithmetic (Morgan Stanley's 5.9x target EV/EBITDA) produces a target of PLN 350, 5 percent above the price; the bull path at 15 percent odds does not lift the probability-weighted return above an F; 'priced' is not 'bounded', since on the same earnings the multiple's own history allows a fall to 5.8x (-40 percent) and the earnings carry a 66 percent sensitivity to a 10 percent copper move; and the risk that is not priced is the one the owner controls, the use of the balance sheet for acquisitions and polyhalite (USD 2 to 5 billion plus up to PLN 10 billion). The competing hypothesis does not need a sum-of-the-parts argument; it needs copper, and a case that is compelling only if copper rises another 50 percent is not a modal case. On the 'Foundations', the counter-case (a deposit with mine plans past 2055, an integrated chain immune to the treatment-charge collapse, the second-largest silver output, no customer above 10 percent of revenue, the NKT contract to 2036 worth EUR 5.4 to 7.0 billion) is conceded in full and answered by the record of the business: the change does not stick (returns of 10 to 11 percent in a record year; negative free cash flow for five years; a 16 percent domestic EBITDA margin; unit costs up 8 percent a year compounded; three chief executive changes in twelve months). The geology is a floor under the company, not a spring under the shares.
triggers: - Re-open the case: copper sustained above USD 16,000 per tonne with the shares below PLN 260; or a change of owner behaviour (an equity-aligned chief executive; a withdrawn polyhalite commitment) with the multiple below 7.4x.

- Copper price (LME, daily): modal flat near USD 14,000 per tonne; above USD 16,000 confirms the bull branch; alarm USD 11,000; invalidate USD 9,000 (below USD 10,000, about USD 4.50 per pound, refutes the earnings base).

- Domestic cost per tonne (quarterly; next 2026-11-18): above PLN 55,000 in Q2 2026; management's target below PLN 50,000 by Q4 2026 is the test of the self-help; alarm PLN 55,000 sustained at Q3 2026; invalidate above PLN 58,000. A Q3 2026 cost per tonne below PLN 52,000 with the anode inventory released would change the record's mind on costs.
- The 24-month-forward multiple (weekly): 9.6x; modal 8.1x; alarm below 7.4x; a multiple holding above 10x through a quarter of flat earnings would say the market has re-based the stock's range.
- Domestic cost structure: alarm a wage settlement above 7 percent; invalidate labour cost +15 percent in FY2027.
- State-directed capital allocation: alarm any supervisory board sweep; invalidate a fourth chief executive; the 2027 parliamentary election is inside the horizon.
